sayLines.line: 📖 LEARNED: Wound Care (Level 2). Honey is antibacterial. Sugar packs wounds. Yarrow stops bleeding. The old ways work.
📖 LEARNED: Calming Panic (Level 2). You can talk someone down from a full panic attack. Voice low, steady, certain. You are the calm.
📖 LEARNED: Managing Fear (Level 2). You can function through terror. Your hands shake but they work. This is a trained skill.
📖 LEARNED: Steady Hands (Level 1). Fine work under pressure. Dressing game, stitching wounds, tying snares — no shake.
📖 Your old life taught you things. 4 skills from your past — check your Journal.

You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Hudson Egan. Army medic. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Field suture kit, Mixtape, Marked Bus Map, Dead Phone, Trail compass. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. They found a deer this morning. Inside out. Not eaten — unmade. Like something was trying to understand how it worked. It didn't finish.
A person, maybe 40s, with thick glasses: "We've got days of stores, not weeks. The treeline is the pantry now. Learn what's out there."
📓 Journal: Food won't come to Haven. Walk past the treeline — learn what grows out there, bring it back, and get it named at camp.
